newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Afghan, Iranian leaders to visit Tajikistan.
newsitem.headline: Afghan, Iranian leaders to visit Tajikistan.

text.p: The presidents of Afghanistan and Iran will visit the former Soviet republic of Tajikistan on Friday to discuss regional security and the Afghan war, a Tajik official said on Wednesday.

"It is expected that the three presidents will discuss issues linked to problems of regional security and a possible peaceful settlement to the Afghan situation," said Zafar Saidov, spokesman for Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov.

Rakhmonov was to hold the meeting on Friday with Afghan President Burhanuddin Rabbani -- driven out of the Afghan capital Kabul by the purist Islamic Taleban militia last September -- and Iranian President Ali Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani.

Tajikistan, like Central Asia's other ex-Soviet republics, is concerned that the Taleban may launch a summer offensive to gain control of northern Afghan territory controlled by anti-Taleban forces of General Abdul Rashid Dostum and commander Ahmad Shah Masood.
Rakhmonov aired worries recently that up to a million refugees could flood his own war-wracked country from northern Afghanistan if hostilities restarted.
Last December, Rakhmonov's secular government and the country's armed Islamist opposition agreed to a ceasefire after four years of civil war.
But the fragile peace is often disturbed by armed maverick bands and drug traders operating out of bases in neighbouring Afghanistan.
